problem: The figure shows an object store as a third metered resource feeding the monitor, but the invoice note ₹482.19 is exactly the total from Worked example 1, which prices only vCPU, RAM and the block volume. A student will look for the missing object-storage charge and find nothing.
fix: Either drop the object-store node from the figure so it matches the worked example, or keep it and give the invoice a total that includes an object-storage line (or note on the figure that the object-store charge is excluded).

problem: Disk is billed only for the 10 hours of the run, yet Exam trap 1 says a stopped VM keeps billing its disk. Nothing in the example says the volume is deleted at the 10-hour mark, so the two statements read as contradictory.
fix: State the assumption in the example: 'the volume exists for exactly these 10 hours and is deleted after the run'. Otherwise show the disk continuing to bill per GB-month after the run stops.

problem: The answer's fix is 'tag every resource, then re-aggregate by tag', but the question says the provider exposes only host-level meters. Host-level totals carry no per-resource records, so tags have nothing to attach to and tagging alone cannot split them.
fix: Add the first step: switch on resource-level metering (provider resource metrics or a guest-level agent) so each VM and volume has its own records, then tag those records with team and env and re-aggregate by tag.

problem: 'Unit 3 covers how' and 'Unit 4 covers how these stores are built' are plain text, so a reader on a phone cannot jump to them; the book's convention is to link other chapters.
fix: Replace each with a link such as Unit 3 (and the matching id for Unit 4).
